chunks: Yet they say that God has begotten a son. May He be praised! Indeed everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, and all are obedient to God.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God having a son?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to refute the Christian doctrine of divine sonship and the concept of intercessors, affirming Allah's absolute transcendence (Tanzih) and unique sovereignty. It underscores that all beings, whether angels or humans, are merely servants (Qanitin) obedient to His will, rejecting any notion of inherent divinity in created entities.
